summary: Ada opens big work with edges, not features: every epic starts by naming what is out of scope before what is in, then cuts the rest into phases that each end at a verification gate. The agent proves a phase (test run, screenshot) before the next begins, and acceptance criteria arrive as observable outcomes rather than adjectives. Bugs get the same discipline in miniature — repro command, observed symptom, suspected file — so the first agent turn is a fix attempt, not a search. Mechanical work is pushed down to subagents; anything irreversible stays in the main thread for review.

traits.title: Scopes out before scoping in
traits.detail: Epics open with an explicit in-scope / out-of-scope split, so the agent never wanders into next quarter's work.

evidence.quote: Out of scope: per-site permissions (next quarter), mobile layout changes.

traits.title: Phases with a verification gate each
traits.detail: Large work is cut into reviewable phases, and the agent must prove each one before the next begins.

evidence.quote: After each phase run the e2e suite and show me a screenshot before moving on.

traits.title: Quality bars are observable, not adjectives
traits.detail: Acceptance criteria are stated as things you could check — which makes "done" checkable too.

evidence.quote: Quality bar: no visible layout shift when switching sites.

traits.title: Anchors bugs to the exact repro
traits.detail: Bug reports carry the repro command, the observable symptom and the suspected file.

evidence.quote: repro: docker restart broker while watching /debug/subs — count goes to 0 and stays

traits.title: Delegates the mechanical, keeps the risky
traits.detail: Subagents get renames and boilerplate; schema changes and anything irreversible stay under review.

evidence.quote: Use subagents for the mechanical renames so the main thread stays focused on the schema changes.

templates.title: Open an epic with edges
templates.prompt:
We're adding <feature> to <project>. Goal: <one-sentence outcome>.

In scope: <a, b, c>. Out of scope: <x (deferred to when)>, <y>.

Work in phases — 1) <phase>, 2) <phase>, 3) <phase>. After each phase run <suite> and show me <proof> before moving on. Quality bar: <observable outcome>.

templates.title: Bug report in four beats
templates.trait: Anchors bugs to the exact repro
templates.prompt: Fix <symptom> in <project>: when <trigger>, <observed behaviour> (repro: <command> while watching <where> — <what you see>). Expected: <behaviour, with a limit>. Suspect <file or path>.

templates.title: Delegate with a stop condition
templates.trait: Delegates the mechanical, keeps the risky
templates.prompt: Plan first, then implement. Break <the work> into steps I can review; after each step run <tests> and stop if anything fails twice in a row. Use subagents for <the mechanical part>. Don't push anything — leave commits local for my review.
